To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have improved the performance (latencies) of the double precision floating-point arithmetic unit by 26.96% by employing our proposed look-up table based algorithms.
we have proposed a new look up table based double precision floating point division algorithm that has better area and timing performance than other look up table based division algorithms.
we have proposed different look up table optimizations to achieve high performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high performance, low area and low power double precision floating point units for embedded applications.
the design of a low cost and high performance double precision floating point division algorithm for embedded systems.
the development of a double precision floating point look up table based arithmetic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have improved the latency x area performance of the double precision floating arithmetic by 26.9% to 30.4% over the state of the art algorithms.
the proposed algorithm is a good candidate for the implementation of double precision floating point division in FPGAs.

the proposed algorithm has the highest performance (latency) and lowest area among all the algorithms in the literature and also has the lowest latency among the look up table based division algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved 1.8x performance improvement in the area and timing trade off of double precision floating point division algorithm.
we improve the performance of double precision floating point division algorithm by 27.3% over Wong and Goto algorithm, and by 15.4% over Goto and Kojima algorithm.
we have improved the performance of Wong and G. division algorithm from 2.4 to 1.8.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can improve the performance of look up table based algorithm significantly with simple optimization techniques.
we can achieve higher performance (latency) with area and power trade off.
, the look up table based algorithm proposed by Wong and Got can be improved further by employing our proposed optimization techniques.
